Libraryライブラリ

Real time, place, depth and magnitude, and the maximum intensity matched to the official record where one exists. Quakes from 2011 on replay the EEW reports JMA actually sent; older ones get simulated reports. The station network is simulated on real ground data. Each one opens as a new project.

Bring in a real earthquake from a live feed, or a scenario someone shared with you. Whatever you import opens as a new project.

Quickest: grab the latest

These buttons work when Quaker runs on a normal website, like the GitHub Pages version. Inside Claude the page is sandboxed and can’t reach other sites, so use copy and paste.

Copy and paste (works everywhere)

  1. Open one of the links below. It opens in a new tab and shows a wall of text. That’s the data.
  2. Select all of it (Ctrl+A, or ⌘+A on a Mac) and copy it (Ctrl+C or ⌘+C). On a phone, long-press the text, then Select All and Copy.
  3. Come back here, paste it into the box below and press Read it.
  4. If the feed has several quakes you get a list. Tap the one you want.
USGSEvery country, updated within minutes. Magnitude, place, depth and time.
M2.5+ past week M4.5+ past month Significant, past month
Older quakes: this search lists M7+ from March 2011. Change the dates and the magnitude in the address bar to find yours.
P2PQuakeJapan, from JMA’s reports, with the shindo each town actually felt. Quaker paints those real intensities onto the map.
Latest 30 quakes
Change limit=30 in the address to anything up to 100 for more.
JMAThe official Japanese list. Pasting it gives you each quake’s place, magnitude and top shindo.
Quake list
For one quake’s full town-by-town intensity, find it in the list, copy its json file name, open www.jma.go.jp/bosai/quake/data/ followed by that name, and paste that page instead.
Quaker codes and filesA code someone shared (it starts with QK2-), or a .json file from Share or a project’s Export. Paste the code in the box, or use Open a file.

Shortcutsショートカット

SpacePlay or pause RRestart from the beginning ← →Seek 5 seconds (hold Shift for 1 second) Home EndJump to start or end JSkip to the intensity report FFullscreen MSound on or off CAuto camera on or off ZDetection zoom on or off AFit every quake, or just the newest LOn-screen language: Japanese broadcast style or English + −Zoom the map ESwitch Easy and Advanced Ctrl+ZUndo (Advanced) Ctrl+Shift+ZRedo (Advanced) DeleteRemove whatever is selected (Advanced) D or Ctrl+DDuplicate the selection (Advanced) Ctrl+ASelect every box, report, camera key and cue (Advanced) [ ]Nudge the selection 0.5 s earlier or later. Hold Shift for 0.1 s (Advanced) SSplit the selected box at the playhead (Advanced) HHide or show the selected boxes (Advanced) Alt+↑ ↓Move a box’s row up or down (Advanced) EscCancel picking, close menus, then let go of the selection , .Jump to the previous or next key moment (detection, warning, report…) IPreview the intro screen OLoop on or off PSave this frame as a picture

On the timeline

Click the rulerMove the playhead there. The colored tags on top are key moments (detection, warning, report). Click one to jump to it. Click empty spaceMove the playhead and let go of the selection Drag empty spaceDraw a box to select everything inside it Shift-clickAdd to or take out of the selection. Dragging one moves them all. Double-click a rowAdd something to that row at that time Right-clickOptions for whatever you clicked. On a phone, press and hold. ▾ on a trackFold the track away. ＋ adds to it, ⋯ has the rest. Alt while draggingTurn snapping off (or on) for that drag Ctrl + scrollZoom the timeline around the pointer

Data: ground amplification from J-SHIS (NIED, V4 site amplification, Vs400 to surface). Travel times from JMA2001 (Ueno et al. 2002, JMA). Real EEW reports from JMA's published record of warnings. Shaking from Si & Midorikawa (1999) and Midorikawa et al. (1999).
